text:
In December 2013 we converged. Forty-two of us said "the bipartisan budget," and thirty-five said "bipartisan budget act," peaking together on 2013-12-12. Thirty-four of us added the article: "the bipartisan budget act." Twenty-eight said "budget act of," and twenty-seven said "the bipartisan budget act of." The first among us to say "the bipartisan budget" was M001185, back on 2013-05-16, months before the rest arrived.

Twenty-seven of us said we did it "without raising taxes." Twenty-six called it a move "in the right direction," and twenty-three of us called it a "step in the right direction," a phrasing first recorded from one of us on 2013-01-15.

We record this not to explain it but to note it: on a single December day, dozens of us reached for the same words at once. The instrument shows the convergence. It does not show the memo.
